| D-REFAV1-KAPPA-BUDGET | ⛔⛔ **THE PLANNER CANNOT AFFORD AN URBAN TURN — ARITHMETICALLY, AT THE SHIPPED WEIGHTS, AND NO AMOUNT OF TRAINING CHANGES IT.** MEASURED 2026-09-04 on the banked step-21,109 dump (282 windows / 141 clusters) plus the two source constants: every emitted plan has κ ≡ 0 and constant `a`, so `W_KAPPA·κ̄² = 0` and `W_JERK·jerk² = 0` **exactly** — i.e. the recorded `plan_cost` IS the goal term alone. Its whole range over the split is mean **1.18e-05**, p90 4.03e-05, **max 1.41e-04** (exactly zero on 113/282). A candidate that bends must repay `W_KAPPA·κ̄²` out of a goal term it can at best drive to zero, so the RMS curvature of ANY winning plan is bounded by `κ* = sqrt(goal_cost / W_KAPPA)`: **0.0155 1/m (R = 65 m) at the mean, and 0.053 1/m (R = 18.8 m) even in the single most goal-dominated window in the entire split.** An urban junction turn (R = 8 m, κ = 0.125) costs **7.81e-04 = 66× the whole mean goal term**; a 6 m turn 118×; the search-box edge `kappa_max = 0.2` costs 170×. ⇒ the bound is a property of the COST, not of the weights, and it is why the tactical decoder asking for a turn on **12/13** labelled TURN windows is executed on **0/13**. | **SUPPORTED (MEASURED, ours)** | `taniteval/tools/refav1_independent_probe.py` on `taniteval/results/refav1-21109-openloop-dump.tar.gz`; constants `stack/tanitad/refs/refa_v1.py:284-285`, applied `:2176-2177` |

`…/2026-09-04-refav1-cost-scale/PROPOSED_REGISTER_ROWS.md` §3):** this clause used to read *"varies by 1.63e-10 along κ against a float32 `1−cos` step of 5.96e-08 (`D-REFAV1-COST-SURFACE`)"* — **(1)** 1.63e-10 is that study's **`incumbent`**-checkpoint figure (its companion checkpoint read 5.82e-08, a 357× spread inside its own table), and at step 21,109 the quantity is **1.2 × 10⁴ × larger** — the difference between the pre-registered *"a deletion, not a weight"* verdict and a tipping `W_KAPPA` of 3.40e-06 that sits 2.28× ABOVE the deletion threshold (0 of 30 per-window tipping weights are deletions); **(2)** float32 does NOT annihilate the signal — the κ sub-box spans **33.3 ulp** and fits inside one ulp on **0.00 %** of windows; what float32 costs is **RESOLUTION** (the argmin over 10 curvature candidates is TIED on **45.4 %** of windows, float64 0.0 %, and disagrees with float64 on 21.6 %); **(3)** that tie rate is the measured mechanism of the `baseline_won_frac` mislabel below: for `cem`-labelled plans whose controls ARE a baseline, `res.cost − min(baseline_costs)` is **exactly −2.00 float32 ulp**, because `base_costs` comes from a SECOND, separate `cost_fn(base_stack)` call (`refa_v1_plan.py:264`) whose batch composition differs and the goal term is a float32 reduction over 65,536 dims — the identical control block scores two ulp apart and fails the `c <= best_cost` relabel. ⛔ **The binding penalty is JERK, not κ²** (99.5 % of the median 0.362 penalty on the searched population; `W_KAPPA = 0` leaves the plan flat, `W_JERK = 0` does not). **SCOPE the row did not carry:** the decoded goal's own canonical controls are exactly zero on **133/282 = 47.2 %** of windows (where `cv` IS the correct plan), want non-zero acceleration on 120/282 = 42.6 % and non-zero curvature on 38/282 = 13.5 % ⇒ **the planner emitted a trivial plan on 149/149 of the windows where its own goal asked for something**, κ ≡ 0 on 38/38 curvature-wanting ones; and the 12 non-flat plans are ANTI-correlated with the goal (0 of the 33 `BRAKE_TO` windows; 12/249 = 4.8 % of the rest; one-sided hypergeometric p = 1). ⇒ **`plan()` is a penalty minimiser; a better-trained network moves nothing, because the defect is in the COST, not the weights** — the verdict STANDS (re-derived independently: κ ≡ 0 on 282/282, accel constant on 282/282, 2 distinct plans, trivial by CONTENT on 282/282), and it is now a theorem about the cost rather than a float32 accident.** ⛔ **INSTRUMENT DEFECT, ESCALATED:** `planner.baseline_won_frac` reads **0.6631** where the truth is **1.0000** — `plan_source` says `cem` on 95 windows and on **95/95** of them the controls are bit-exactly an injected baseline (cross-tab banked). Both tie-break repairs are gated on the LABEL, not the content (`refa_v1_plan.py:277-281`, `refa_v1.py:2203`), so neither fires. **`plan_source` is not evidence about what produced a plan; the CONTENT of the controls is.** ⚠️ **NOT an indictment of the trained model** — three arms in the same record DO read the weights and two are positive (see `D-REFAV1-EPOCH-HEADS`). | **SUPPORTED (MEASURED 2026-09-04, ArchInf FlyWheel; rollout on Thor 3.03 h, analysis 0 GPU; n = 282 windows / 141 episode clusters; two independent probes agree and the renderer refuses if they do not)** | `taniteval/results/RESULT-refav1-21109-openloop.md` · `refav1-21109-openloop.json` · `refav1-21109-openloop-identity.json` · `refav1-21109-openloop-extra.json` (the `plan_source` × controls-content cross-tab) · `refav1-21109-openloop-dump.tar.gz` · `openloop-suite-refav1-21109.*` (criteria registry v2.5.0: **0 violations, 3 work items**, `const0` OK) · cross-box confirmation on a different GPU: `refav1-21109-openloop-devbox-crosscheck.json` (14/14) · instrument `taniteval/tools/refav1_openloop_report.py` + `stack/tests/test_refav1_openloop_report.py` (12 tests) |

| D-REFAV1-COST-SCALE | ⭐⭐ **THE FLAT PLAN IS A THEOREM ABOUT THE COST — provable without the world model, and therefore not fixable by training, by a checkpoint, or by a weight.** The goal term is non-negative, so a candidate beats `cv` only if `penalty(n) < goal(cv)`. confirmed in the sweep, where `W_KAPPA = 0` with jerk shipped is STILL flat and `W_JERK = 0` with `W_KAPPA` shipped is not. ⭐ **AND THE WORLD-MODEL TERM IS SIGNAL, NOT A DEGENERACY**: paired magnitude-matched contrasts with episode-cluster intervals give TURN_L lift **+0.50221 [+0.38348, +0.57927] SEPARATED**, TURN_R **−0.38725 [−0.49764, −0.26686] SEPARATED**, against a LANE_KEEP control at **−0.01254 [−0.02581, +0.00079]** (straddles 0); longitudinally ACCELERATE **+0.577**, BRAKE_TO **−0.826**, CRUISE **−0.0035**. **A working, correctly-signed, goal-conditioned predictor is being outvoted by two unnormalised penalties.** | **SUPPORTED (MEASURED 2026-09-04, ArchInf FlyWheel; n = 282 windows / 141 clusters, same grid and same ckpt as `refav1-21109-openloop`; Thor + dev-box RTX 4060; NO retraining, NO weight change — inference-time re-evaluation; ⛔ OPEN LOOP, the planner feeds its own predictor)** — applied to the register 2026-09-05 from the package's `PROPOSED_REGISTER_ROWS.md` §1 | `TanitAD Research Lab/Architecture & Inference/Research/2026-09-04-refav1-cost-scale/RESULT.md` §0, §2c–2d, §4a · `raw/cost_anatomy_full.json` (282 windows) · `raw/cost_sweep_main.json` (the iCEM sweep) |

| D-REFAV1-COST-FORM | ⭐⭐ **RE-FORM, NOT RE-BALANCE — and "normalise the model term" is NOT enough, which is PROVED rather than argued.** `‖(x − x_cv) − (g − x_cv)‖ ≡ ‖x − g‖`, so centring changes an L2 **distance** by exactly nothing; measured, `abs_l2`, `rel_l2`, `boxnorm` and `goalnorm` all read the **identical 0.811 %** L/R decision share and all leave **100.00 %** of the iCEM population a-priori excluded. Only a **DIRECTION comparison in centred space** removes the common mode: `1 − cos(z_K − z_K⁰, g − z_K⁰)` takes the a-priori exclusion **100 % → 1.67 %** and the L/R decision share **1.4 % → 41.3 %**, with `z_K⁰` = the terminal field under zero controls, which the planner **already rolls** as the `cv` baseline (no extra rollout, no privileged information). Under that form the SHIPPED `W_JERK = 0.02` is **0.36× its cap** (i.e. already fine) and `W_KAPPA = 0.05` is if anything **too small**. ⛔ **THE PRICE, STATED BEFORE THE RECOMMENDATION:** `ccos(cv) = 1.0` exactly on 40/40 — the do-nothing candidate scores the worst possible value **by definition**, and on a HOLD goal the goal's own centred vector is float32-noise (‖g − z_K⁰‖/‖z_K⁰‖ = **4.18e-08**), so the comparison degenerates on the majority stratum (LANE_KEEP = 244/282 = 86.5 %). **A centred form must carry an explicit HOLD branch or it trades one degeneracy for another.** ⇒ this is a **PRE-REGISTRATION item** (`TanitAD_ValidateAIDesign` ladder: deliberate-regression arm = the uncentred form; controls = LANE_KEEP must read the no-information value and a constant-only candidate must read a known value), **not a change to ship from this document.** | **PROPOSED — the FORM comparison is SUPPORTED (MEASURED 2026-09-04, n = 40 windows / 20 clips, dev-box RTX 4060, same step-21,109 ckpt: byte size 2,122,997,633 identical to Thor's, labels md5 `aa12c948f062181c3297265b51526ec5` identical to the banked run); the REPAIR itself is UNVALIDATED and gated on a pre-registration** — applied to the register 2026-09-05 from the package's `PROPOSED_REGISTER_ROWS.md` §2 | `TanitAD Research Lab/Architecture & Inference/Research/2026-09-04-refav1-cost-scale/RESULT.md` §4b–4d, §7 · `raw/cost_forms_devbox.json` (40 windows) |

| E-DEC-9b | ⛔⛔ **THE v7f RECIPE DOES NOT CLOSE THE SELF-GENERATED-TARGET PROBLEM — IT NARROWS IT, AND THE ONE TERM THAT MEASURABLY CLOSED IT IS SWITCHED OFF** | ⭐⭐ **MEASURED (from source) + PUBLISHED-PRIMARY** | Term-by-term on `PREREG_V7F` §9's launch line against E-DEC-7's own test: **O5 `--o5-target ema`** → self-generated (E-DEC-13 REFUTED the EMA route in both published forms); **O6** → isotropy, satisfied exactly by noise; **LDAD (proposed)** → its target `(a, κ)` **IS the ego's measured motion** (E-DEC-57, r 0.9988), i.e. the degenerate optimum's own content — a self-generated target wearing a label's clothes; **trunk anchor** → a frozen deepcopy of the model's **OWN SEED** (`build_trunk_anchor(… stack.encoder …)`, taken after `apply_encoder_seed`), which **preserves and cannot supply** (E-DEC-17: a frozen empty field is an empty field) and which **inherits the random `pos` verbatim**; **O7** → the only term that ever put the scene in (E-DEC-8 `n_agents` −1.0407 → **+0.3274**) and v7f sets **`--w-o7-distill 0`**. ⭐ **THE FIELD SETTLES THE CO-TRAINING QUESTION ON OUR EXACT SHAPE:** `lib:2509.10156` (LayerLock) **Table 3** — a self-generated-target latent loss added to an external pixel loss **as a weighted sum** drove SSv2 **50.1 → 3.7**, and **BOTH weight schedules (constant 3.7, cosine 5.6) collapsed**; only **staging with freezing** worked. ⇒ **a `w`-sweep is measured not to be the fix**, and our own E-DEC-12 (+0.1327 staged vs −0.2553 co-trained) and E-DEC-14b-R (+0.3881 frozen vs −0.0180 trainable) are the same result twice. ⚠️ `lib:2302.14138` Table 1: the **ORDER** of staging matters more than the staging itself (+8.9 right order, **15.1 BELOW joint** wrong order) — a staged v7 arm must pre-register its order and carry the reversed order as its deliberate-regression arm.  · **evidence:**  `…/2026-09-04-v7-seed-and-external-target/RESULT.md` §3; `…/2026-09-04-v7-external-target-dominance/LIT_SOTA.md` |

| D-V7-NAVZERO | ⛔ **THE v7 NAV `none` CONTROL IS A ZERO-COLLISION: it is a constant-`NAV_FOLLOW_ROAD` arm, not an ablation** | ⭐ **MEASURED (from source) 2026-09-04 — LATENT, never yet used** | `apply_nav_control(…, "none")` returns `torch.zeros_like(token_id)` (`tanitad/models/nav_conditioning.py:240`) and `NAV_COMMAND_TOKENS[0]` is **`NAV_FOLLOW_ROAD`** (`tanitad/models/vocab_v7.py:331`) — the modal command on a driving corpus. `channel_active=False` is returned but `NavConditioner.embed` has only **3** slots, so the model is still told "follow road". ⇒ the `none` ablation would **manufacture** the conclusion "nav buys nothing". **Two probes confirm no caller** anywhere in `stack/` or `taniteval/` and no `--nav-control` argparse entry, so this is a defect to fix BEFORE it is quoted, not a retraction. **Fix: a 4th `NAV_NONE` slot, or a validity flag concatenated to the embedding.** ⭐ `PUBLISHED-PRIMARY`: an explicit missingness indicator is the field's standard fix and helps **even under MCAR** (`lib:2407.19804`, which names our exact defect — a constant imputation BECOMES the missingness code); `lib:2511.13079` prices zeroed ego velocity at an **8.7× planning degradation**.  · **evidence:**  `…/2026-09-04-v7-seed-and-external-target/RESULT.md` X5 |

| LIT-1 | ⭐⭐ **E-DEC-7 IS INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED BY PUBLISHED WORK — PhyLatent (ICLR 2025) states our root cause almost verbatim** | **PUBLISHED (primary, banked: `TanitAD Research Lab/Library/papers/2608.05720_PhyLatent-…pdf`, 16 pp)** | its abstract: *"preventing global latent collapse does not ensure that a representation preserves physical states and action consequences"* — which is E-DEC-7, arrived at independently by us from measurement. It names three failure modes: **physical invariance collapse, physical identifiability collapse, counterfactual dynamics collapse**, and reports 15.60/6.71/8.41 % → 7.53/0.95/4.62 %, with MPC success 70.0 → 78.1 % on OGBench-Cube and 81.0 → **98.0 %** on TwoRooms. ⇒ **our year of "raise the rank" was optimising a property the literature also finds insufficient.** It is corroboration, not novelty — and it means the remedy space is already mapped |

| LIT-2 | ⭐ **PhyLatent's PSG is the validated form of the supervised scene aux, and it is BINDING-COMPLIANT** | **PUBLISHED — adopt as E-DEC-8(b)'s design** | **Physical State Grounding**: a SHARED state head `H_s` applied to BOTH the encoded trajectory and the predicted continuation, `L_state = MSE(H_s(Z), S̄) + MSE(H_s(Ẑ), S̄)`, with per-dimension z-scored targets. Sharing the head across both branches "gives both representations a common physical interpretation". ⭐ **"The physical targets supervise representation learning only during training and are not required by the planner"** — exactly our binding rule *labels may use ego and other agents; INFERENCE IS VISION-ONLY*. Our banked 3D agent cuboids (`obstacle.offline`, 97.44 % coverage) are the physical targets |

| LIT-3 | ⭐⭐ **PhyLatent's CASC explains AND fixes H-PROOF-4: our O1 moves BOTH branches; theirs STOP-GRADIENTS the factual one** | **PUBLISHED — the concrete fix for the O1 defect** | *"The factual prediction is treated as a **stop-gradient reference**, so this loss separates the counterfactual branch **without moving the factual branch**."* ⇒ **that is precisely why our O1 made the predictor directionally indistinguishable from noise (H-PROOF-4, z −0.26…0.37) while maximising action response**: our anti-echo term let the separation gradient move the FACTUAL prediction too, so the model bought diversity by corrupting correctness. Two further guards we lack: a **margin proportional to the action difference** (`m = min(γ·δa, m_max)`), and applying the loss **only where δa exceeds the batch median**, so near-identical actions are never pushed apart. ⇒ **O1 is not inherently harmful — ours was mis-specified.** Re-registering it as a candidate with the stop-grad + margin + median-gate, rather than "keep O1 off" |

hours ago.** `postrain10k` → `postrain30k` is **the same recipe, the same

`--init-from`, the same everything except training length**, and its drift goes

**0.359 → 0.669**. There is no label standing for a bundle here: the only variable

is how long the encoder trained.



⇒ **TRAINED ENCODERS CONVERGE TO drift ≈ 0.62–0.68** — six of seven trained arms,

spanning **7.5k to 30k steps and BOTH initialisations**, land in a 0.06-wide band.

**Frozen encoders do not** (0.199, 0.337).



⭐⭐ **THE MECHANISM, AND IT IS THE DEEPEST EXPLANATION THIS CAMPAIGN HAS

PRODUCED.** O5 trains the predictor so that `ẑ_{t+k} ≈ z_{t+k}`. When the ENCODER

is trainable, the cheapest way to satisfy that is not to predict better — it is to

make the LATENT ITSELF EASIER TO PREDICT, i.e. smooth and self-predictable.

⇒ **Joint training under O5 MANUFACTURES the drift the programme has spent three

nights trying to remove.** Freezing the encoder removes the degree of freedom that

allows it.



⇒ **This explains the ten failed objectives as a class, and better than E-DEC-48b

did.** Every one of them was bolted onto an O5 that was, in parallel, optimising the

encoder toward exactly the property those terms were fighting. **They were not

merely mining an empty seam — they were mining against an active pump.**

produced nothing. ⇒ Fixed by **K-fold fit + per-clip score** (`panel_kfold.py`):

the t-test needs per-CLIP scores, but **the FIT does not have to be per-clip** —

10 fits instead of 129, the same 129 scores, clip-disjointness preserved. **13×

cheaper, same statistic.** ⚠️ It is a different estimator, so its null was

re-measured under the identical scheme — which is why the 4.15 above is not the

**The channels, from `physicalai.py:604-632` (read from source):**



```

actions[:,0] = steer = atan(wheelbase · curvature)   ← from the `curvature` channel

actions[:,1] = accel = ax                            ← measured longitudinal accel

poses[:,2]   = yaw   = quaternion_yaw(qx,qy,qz,qw)   ← a different sensor path

poses[:,3]   = v     = hypot(vx, vy)

```



Kinematically `yaw_rate = v·κ` and `κ = tan(steer)/L`, so `Δyaw(t→t+k) ≈

v_t·tan(steer_t)/L·k·dt` needs **no learning at all**. The test compares that

closed form against the learned probe:



| relation | r |

|---|---|

| `steer_t` vs **measured** yaw-rate | +0.7826 |

| **closed form `v·tan(steer)/L` vs measured yaw-rate** | **+0.9988** |

| `steer_t` vs Δyaw(t→t+4) | +0.7967 |

| **closed form vs Δyaw(t→t+4)** | **+0.9923** |

| the LEARNED probe (E-DEC-50) | **+0.5638** |



⛔ **r = 0.9988 is not "largely kinematic" — it is an IDENTITY TO THREE DECIMALS.**

The corpus's `curvature` is the measured yaw-rate divided by speed; `steer` is a

re-parameterisation of it. ⇒ **The learned probe was a LOSSY estimator (0.5638) of

a relation computable exactly with no data (0.9923).**

⭐⭐⭐ **THE METHODOLOGICAL RESULT IS BIGGER THAN THE OBJECTIVE RESULT.** Read the

`o5` (o13) column alone: **0.0575 → 0.0195, monotonically falling.** That is what

healthy training looks like, and every diagnostic *inside* the arm agreed —

`o13_excess` positive in all six blocks, the shuffled control sitting at its floor,

`zhat` beating passthrough throughout. **I would have reported success.** The

matched control shows the identical recipe reaches **0.0067** without the term:

the arm's "improvement" is **a third of what it would have achieved by doing

nothing.** ⇒ **A FALLING LOSS CURVE IS NOT EVIDENCE. It is evidence only relative

to a matched arm**, and this is the cleanest demonstration of that in the

programme.



⛔ **THE PRE-REGISTERED CONSEQUENCE, APPLIED AS WRITTEN.**

`PREREG_O13_EGO_DYNAMICS.md` §4, committed **before** this ran: *"`o13_excess > 0`

while `o5` degrades ≥ 10 % → **DEGENERATE**. O13 is **abandoned, not retuned**,

and logged as the tenth failed objective."* The criterion fired at **19× its

threshold**. ⇒ **`o13p30k` is NOT launched.** The staged trainer, the gated

launcher and the md5 verification all remain on Thor, unused.



⚠️ **THE RATIONALISATION I AM DECLINING TO MAKE, STATED SO THE PI CAN OVERRULE ME.**

O13's loss is O(1) while `o5` is O(0.02), so at `--w-o13-ego 0.1` the new term

carries **~5× the weight of the objective it competes with** — the degeneracy may

be MIS-SCALING rather than something fundamental. That is a real observation and I

am recording it. **But "it's degenerate, maybe with a smaller weight…" is exactly

how nine objectives consumed this campaign**, and the pre-registration says

*abandoned, not retuned* precisely to stop me. ⇒ **A weight sweep is a NEW

hypothesis and needs its own pre-registration and its own cheapest discriminating

experiment — not a quiet retune of an abandoned one. It is a PI call, not mine.**

Ten objective terms have now failed (O1, O2, O3, O7, O8, O9, O10, O11, PSG, O13),

(Δspeed t 2.56, Δyaw t 4.57), through **a readout the action cannot reach**, on **a

rather than by argument.

⇒ **THE REDESIGN THE ORACLE DICTATED, and it is strictly better:** the readout

sees **ONLY `zhat_{t+k}`** — not the action (echo closed by construction), not

`z_t` (passthrough closed by construction). **The action's only path to the loss

is THROUGH THE PREDICTOR**, so the gradient can only fall by making the PREDICTED

LATENT carry the ego's future dynamics — which is precisely the missing property.

That is ActSWM's frozen-readout guard (arXiv 2607.26712) applied to a target with

MEASURED information behind it, rather than to a separation score that can be

manufactured. Pre-registered: `PREREG_O13_EGO_DYNAMICS.md`.

*"underpowered by construction, not absence"*. The panel therefore ran a **balanced

joint** (PCA-32 of the latent + the 2 action scalars, **basis fit on the training

folds only**) and reports both. ⭐ The calibration that proves the caveat was real:

on the IDENTITY target, which the action determines exactly, `joint_raw` reads

"the latent hurts", which is a dimensionality artefact, not a finding.

⭐⭐⭐ **THE THREE FACTS THAT COMPOSE INTO THE ANSWER:**

   0.9988**, so `steer` IS the measured yaw-rate in other units and the probe's

   0.5638 was a lossy estimate of it. ⇒ **No surviving evidence that the action

   channel carries ego information at all.** *(kept below as the record)*

   ~~**The action determines the ego's own future — on Δyaw (t 4.57).**~~

   ⛔ **Δspeed (t 2.56) is RETRACTED by E-DEC-56**: the measured null for this panel

   reaches 3.49 and P(null ≥ 2.56) = **0.067**. The surviving channel is the

   **kinematic** one (steer → yaw-rate), so the physics reading is unchanged in

   kind; the longitudinal half is gone. **Echo-cleared:** the corpus's `accel` is the dataset's OWN measured

   `ax` (`physicalai.py:604-632` states verbatim it is *not* a finite difference of

   v), and `r(accel, realised Δv_1tick) = +0.326` — nowhere near the ~1.0 an

   identity would give.

   better than chance, but **6 seeds cannot quantify it.** ⇒ **Downgraded to

3. ⛔ **The PREDICTOR adds nothing on any ego target, in either arm.** `zhat`

   never exceeds `z_t`, and on `splitp30k`'s Δspeed it **destroys** it

⇒ ⭐⭐⭐ **NINE OBJECTIVES ASKED THE ACTION TO MOVE THE SCENE LATENT — where

E-DEC-48b proves it has NO information. The action's measurable causal content is

the EGO's own dynamics, and no objective has ever used that as a target.** This is

the constructive complement to E-DEC-48b: that result said what the action cannot

do, this one says what it *can*, and both are held-out and controlled.



⇒ **O13 — the EGO-DYNAMICS objective:** predict Δ(speed, yaw) at t+k from

`(z_t, action_t)`. Action-conditioning aimed at the one quantity the action

demonstrably determines, on a subspace the encoder demonstrably already has.

⭐ The Δyaw relation is **largely KINEMATIC** (steer = atan(L·curvature),

yaw-rate ≈ v·curvature), so r +0.56 is **not an empirical discovery** — it is

exactly the closed-form driving physics the mandate names, which makes it the

cleanest possible target: a deterministic function of quantities the encoder

already carries, that the transition still fails to compute.

ego's command carries no information about how other traffic evolves beyond what

the present scene already carries.



⭐⭐⭐ **THIS EXPLAINS NINE FAILURES AT ONCE.** O1, O2, O3, O7, O8, O9, O10, O11 and

PSG did not fail because they were badly designed — **they asked the model to

extract information that observational driving data does not contain.** It is also

why O11 could only manufacture separation (E-DEC-30/C151) and why Δz's residual is

noise in all 8 arms (E-DEC-40/42).



⚠️⚠️ **SCOPE — THIS REFRAMES MANDATE 3, IT DOES NOT CLOSE IT.** The panel measures

the action's contribution to predicting **OTHER AGENTS**. It does **NOT** test its

contribution to predicting the **EGO'S OWN** future state, which the action

certainly determines. ⇒ **The causal arrow in driving data runs SCENE → ACTION,

not ACTION → SCENE.** Other traffic evolves largely independently of what we do.



⇒ *"If the lead decelerates, the ego must react"* is **not a statement the WORLD

MODEL should encode — it is one the PLANNER should.** The world model should

predict the scene from the scene; **action-conditioning belongs on the EGO

TRAJECTORY** (hypothesis H3 in `ACTION_CONDITIONING_HYPOTHESES.md`), which this

result strengthens rather than refutes.



⚠️ **What would still change this:** a corpus with INTERVENTIONAL action diversity

(the same scene paired with different actions — simulation, or AlpaSim). That is a

PI-level provisioning call, not a loss change.

| E-DEC-5 | The environment gap is an objective gap that O2/O3 can close | ⛔ **REFUTED for the O2/O3 route (see E-DEC-5b); the OBJECTIVE-GAP diagnosis itself stands and moves to E-DEC-8** | across every arm measured, **not one** carries agent-count or lead-gap above a constant predictor, while a frozen encoder that never saw our data reads +0.2754 on `n_agents`. Adding O3 runs against our OWN measured finding, and **H-PROOF-4** showed exactly how adding a term (O1) destroyed the predictor while raising its apparent activity. ⇒ **KILL-GATE, committed in advance: an O3 arm is REJECTED if participation falls below the `rdw8` baseline on BOTH held-out sets, or if directional cos vs the permutation null drops to z < 2, EVEN IF environment decodability improves.** The panel must report, together: participation (val AND held24), mean-centred cos + permutation z, ego decodability, environment decodability. Measuring environment alone would reproduce the O1 mistake in a new costume — a term that buys the thing being measured while destroying the thing that was working |

If flow were the source, ego decodability would collapse. It **does not**: speed **+0.2830 → +0.3115 (t +2.37, 10/12 — it slightly IMPROVES)**, `d_ego` +0.3601 → +0.3558 (t −0.20, not separable). ⇒ **ego is read from SINGLE-FRAME APPEARANCE** (motion blur, and scene type correlating with speed), not from inter-frame motion. ⭐ Practical consequence: the `nstack1` arm — which crashed on Thor because the cache has 9 frame channels baked in, so `n_stack=1` is a cache REBUILD not a flag — **is not worth rebuilding**. The no-new-term route via the frame stack is closed |

| H-PROOF-3b | *(instrument)* A single shuffled-target draw is not a leakage floor | **SUPPORTED — my own control was mis-thresholded** | the first decomposition voided its only signal-bearing row because one shuffle read **0.0527** against a hard threshold of 0.05. Mean-centring (correctly applied, and it did move the numbers) reduced it only 0.0664 → 0.0527, which was the clue. ⇒ **a shuffle control must be a DISTRIBUTION (≥100 draws, report z and p), never a single draw against a guessed constant** — otherwise the control manufactures false negatives exactly where the signal is, which is the mirror image of C-2026-08-22's false positives |

Nothing invented. ⚠️ **What it removes, PER LAYER, and why the arm is a LOWER BOUND**: tactical (E13 `PhiTac`) REMOVED entirely and strategic (E13 `ctx`) REMOVED entirely (both guarded on `nav_cmd is not None`, `refc_v3.py:437–441`; `nav_injected` reads False) — but the **CORE measurement encoder is NOT removed, it COLLAPSES onto the majority token** (`one_hot(0)` = `follow`, `refc.py:2021–2024`), because `NAV_COMMANDS` has no `unknown` and the companion bit is off, so “no nav” and “a genuine follow” are BYTE-IDENTICAL there. ⇒ **`os_navzero` UNDERSTATES nav dependence**, and that is stated in the tool, the doc and the record. ⚠ **DECLARED SEPARATELY — ONE INSTRUMENT WAS CORRECTED, AND IT HAD NEVER RUN.** `refc_sampler.assert_matches_diffusers` carried `atol = 1e-10` and **could never have passed**; it had never executed because `diffusers` was never installed beside it. Installed **diffusers 0.40.0** (`--no-deps`; torch verified unchanged at **2.11.0+cu128, `cuda True`, via a real CUDA `conv2d`**) and it raised at **1.689e-07** — a **DTYPE** comparison, not an error: `DDIMScheduler` builds its table in **float32**, `DDIMSchedule` in float64. MEASURED: ours-f32 vs diffusers-f32 **0.000e+00 (bit-equal)**; ours-f64 vs an exact f64 reference **6.939e-18**; **diffusers-f32 vs that reference 1.689e-07** — **ours is the more accurate of the two**. A tolerance below the reference's own epsilon is not a strict test but an **unrunnable** one, the mirror image of a guard that cannot fail. The replacement is **STRICTER**: it rebuilds our schedule at the reference's dtype and requires **BIT-EQUALITY** (passes, no tolerance), then bounds the f64 residual at `16 × eps` because a 1000-step `cumprod` accumulates (measured gap **1.42 × eps**). ⇒ The schedule is now **PRIMARY-verified against the published reference**.

⛔ **A NEW VARIANCE OBLIGATION.** `_sample` draws fresh noise **at eval as well as training** — by design, because sampling is the mechanism. refcv5 is therefore a **STOCHASTIC PLANNER** and `D-REFAV1-SEED-GOAL-MISMATCH` binds: the same checkpoint evaluated twice does not give the same answer (that rig's inference-seed floor was **≈0.30 m ADE**). ⇒ **Any refcv5 sampler result needs INFERENCE-seed replicates**; the episode-cluster bootstrap is structurally blind to this. Written into the `_sample` docstring so it travels with the code.

⚠ **A CONFIG DECISION THE TRAINING OWNER MUST MAKE, NOT A BUG.** `SelectionConfig.refined` defaults to **False**, so the ranked score is the CLASSIFIER surface — which the sampler deliberately does not touch. With it False the fan is **SAMPLED but RANKED by a head that never saw the sample**, which is the S1 defect one level up (measured there as a 45.4 %-of-windows ranking failure). **Stamped, not refused** — "improve the geometry, keep the ranking" is a legitimate arm — via the new telemetry key **`sampler_ranks_the_fan`**. ⇒ **An arm that wants the sampler to reach SELECTION must run `--sel-refined`.**

⛔⛔ **AND THE DELIBERATE REGRESSION COULD NOT HAVE FAILED — CAUGHT IN MY OWN CODE.** `sampler_space="metre"` is pre-registered to FAIL the flyability gate; the first implementation used `metre_sigma_m` **as a divisor**, delivering `sigma(8) x 0.90 = 0.028 m` of noise — **31.7x too gentle** — so the DD-literal arm would have PASSED the gate it exists to fail. **An arm that cannot fail proves nothing**, the same defect this seam is instrumented against, one level down. The normaliser is now DERIVED (`metre_sigma_m / sqrt(1 - abar(infer_t))` = 28.49 / 23.11) so the noise IS DD's published 0.90 m / 0.73 m, and the field is renamed so it cannot be misread as a divisor again. **MEASURED after the fix** (zero-init head, implied |a_lat| between 0.5 s slots): `control` mean **0.5312 m/s²**, max 1.7395 (0.18 g), **0.0000 over mu = 0.7**; `metre` mean **5.2941 m/s²**, max 16.1573 (1.65 g), **0.3333 over mu = 0.7**. ⭐ The design plan predicted ~5.8 m/s² for DD's 0.73 m over a 0.5 s slot and the arm reads 5.29 — the prediction reproduces, and *flyable by construction* is now a MEASUREMENT rather than a claim. Pinned by `test_metre_space_arm_is_UNFLYABLE_and_the_control_arm_is_NOT`.

⭐ **`CRITERIA_REGISTRY.md` v2.7.0 → v2.8.0** adds **`hyg.inference_seed`** with its deliberate-regression arm and a control: a SAMPLING planner must report its inference-seed replicate and seed floor, or refuse with a reason. | | |
|---|---|
| **writer** | `taniteval/tools/refcv3_arm.py:2633` → `ref.setdefault("_defects", []).append(...)`, and `ref` becomes `rec["refcv3"]` (`:2445`, `:2712`) |
| **reader** | `taniteval/tools/run_hierarchy_panel.py:71` → `rec.get("_defects")` — **TOP LEVEL** |

**MUTATION PROOF** (`raw/prove_defect_blind.out`), three arms, both controls behaving:

| arm | record shape | `record_ok()` |
|---|---|---|
| **A** | the defect where the writer **actually puts it** | ⛔ **`True` — "parses, no defects"** |
| **B** *(control)* | the same defect at `rec["_defects"]` | ✅ `False` — caught |
| **C** *(control)* | genuinely clean | ✅ `True` |

⛔ **All three guards over it are blind, and two are source-string matches rather than behaviour:**
`run_hierarchy_panel.record_ok` (wrong scope); `panel_preflight.check_defect_classifier` (asserts the
**writer's text exists**, never that a reader reads that path); and
`test_navcomp_labels_shape.py::test_the_record_marks_the_block_and_collects_it_at_the_top_level` —
**the test's NAME asserts "at the top level"; its assertion is the same source string, which puts it
one level down.** `refcv3_arm.py` itself never exits non-zero on `_defects`.

⭐ **The measured consequence** (`raw/criteria_census.out`, `tools/criteria_check.py --all`,
registry v2.7.0, 87 artifacts → **39 in scope**): the STRATEGIC behavioural family reads
**0 present · 1 refused · 38 MISSING** on `nav_compliance` **and both of its controls** — it has
**never once been produced**, and no gate ever stopped a panel over it. *(Corpus totals: 493 silent
omissions, 61 work items, 7 UNSTAMPED tiers, 20 UNKNOWN scope.)*

**Fix (one line + one test):**
`defects = (rec.get("_defects") or []) + ((rec.get("refcv3") or {}).get("_defects") or [])`,
plus a **behavioural** regression test that plants the defect **at the writer's path** and asserts
`record_ok() is False`. *(Class: guards-need-mutation-not-inspection; and it fails by the SAME
mechanism — a path/scope mismatch — as the `os.path.exists(<dict>)` bug it was written to prevent.)*

### `D-REFCV5-PHANTOM-SEAMS` — ⛔ **SEVEN phantom seam keys: the dead-flag defect is a CLASS, not one flag**

`D-REFCV5-WP4-CONFIG-ONLY` found that `--sampler ddim` stamps a mechanism that does not exist.
**Sweeping the whole argv→`config.json` path** (`_seam_stamp` AST-walked; every
`getattr(core.decoder, "<name>", …)` checked against `DecoderConfig`'s real dataclass fields —
`raw/sweep_phantom_stamps.out`):

| stamped key | real `DecoderConfig` field? |
|---|---|
| `feasible_decode` · `feasible_mu` · `feasible_entry` · `feasible_a_max` · `feasible_kappa_max` · `feasible_prefix_slots` | ✅ **REAL** (6) — Stage 0's wiring is genuine |
| `sampler` · `sampler_space` · `sampler_steps` · `sampler_infer_t` · `sampler_groups` · `cross_agent` · `control_norm` | ⛔ **PHANTOM** (7) |

`DecoderConfig` is **not frozen**, so `setattr(dc, "sampler", "STAMPED_BUT_UNREAD")` is accepted for
all seven: the pin creates an ad-hoc attribute, `_seam_stamp` reads it back, and `config.json`
records a **truthful-looking provenance line for a mechanism with no code behind it**. Converse
control: `feasible_decode` IS a declared field ⇒ the sweep is not vacuous.
**Fix:** `@dataclass(frozen=True)` (or stamp only `dataclasses.fields()`), shipped with this sweep
as its test, so an unknown seam raises at pin time.

### `D-REFCV5-SUPERVISION-N-IS-WINDOWS` — ⛔ **"n = 2,400 instead of n = 190" is a CLIP count; the CE is per WINDOW and the figure is 23.30 %**

`v7_labels.window_in_band` admits a window only when `|t_now − t0| ≤ (hi−lo)/2`. With
`bands.tactical_s = [2.0, 6.0]` and `t0_s = 8.0` on **all 2,400 records** (one label per clip), the
admitted NOW is **[6.0, 10.0] s** of a ~20 s episode. MEASURED on the **real** local parity v2 cache
through the trainer's own dataset arithmetic (`raw/inband_windows.out`; controls:
`window_in_band(8.0)` **True**, `(0.0)` **False**):

```
windows/episode 176.0    in-band/episode 41.0
TOTAL 16,893   SUPERVISED 3,936  = 23.30 %   (76.70 % carry IGNORE_ID -100)
```

⚠️ Scope: 96/2,400 clips are local (4.0 %); the figure is **structural, not sampled** — one `t0_s`,
one band, episode length 198–200 frames.
⭐ **The trainer already knows this distinction and applies it to the OTHER join** —
`enable_agent_join` computes *"NOW-frame coverage over THIS dataset's own window index … Clip
coverage is not supervision coverage"* (`refc_v3_train.py:885-888, 921-922`) — while the **v7 label
join computes only clip coverage** and floors on that.
✅ The `IGNORE_ID` design is **SOUND** (never clamps to a neutral class; half-width derived from the
record's own bands, so the `HORIZON` derived-constant trap is handled correctly). The defect is only
in **which number is published**. **Fix:** compute and stamp the NOW-frame coverage for `v7_by_sid`
and quote *it* as the supervision `n`.

### `D-REFCV5-EVAL-LABEL-FLOOR-MISSING` — ⛔ **the eval-side label join has NO coverage floor**

Exactly one floor exists in the trainer: `refc_v3_train.py:2632`, `if frac < 0.5: raise SystemExit`,
on the **train** side. The `--eval-labels` block (`:2694-2701`) builds `e_ds.v7_by_sid` and
**computes no coverage and applies no floor**. An eval-label blob covering ~0 % of the eval cache is
accepted silently, and the in-training TACTICAL/STRATEGIC families would then be computed over almost
no labelled windows while the run looked labelled — **the same hole the train-side floor exists to
close, on the half that produces the numbers.** **Fix:** lift the identical four lines.

### `D-REFCV5-DIFFUSERS-PIN-CANNOT-PASS` — ⛔ **the one independent check on WP-4's schedule math has never certified anything**

The schedule math is reported as WP-4's sound half, *"its load-bearing identity pinned"*.
`refc_sampler.assert_matches_diffusers` exists because *"a re-implementation that is never checked is
just an unverified copy"*. MEASURED (`raw/diffusers_pin_rootcause.out`):

| quantity | value |
|---|---|
| our `alphas_cumprod` dtype | **float64** |
| `diffusers` `alphas_cumprod` dtype | **float32** |
| measured disagreement | **1.689e-07** |
| declared `atol` | **1e-10** |
| float32 eps | **1.192e-07** ⇒ the error is **1.42× float32 eps** |

⇒ a float64 table compared against a float32 table at a tolerance ~1,000× below float32's
representable precision. It has exactly two outcomes, neither a certification: **SKIP** where
`diffusers` is absent (how it has read as "passing") or **FAIL** where it is present (this box).
⭐ Same family as `D-REFCV5-DEFECT-GATE-BLIND` — a control whose verdict is set by its configuration
rather than by the thing it measures. **Fix:** compare in a common dtype and set `atol` reachable in
the lower precision (~1e-6), naming the dtype in the message.

### `D-REFAV1-TAC-DECODER` — the lateral head IS the constant predictor, to the digit



**MEASURED, T0, 140 windows / 20 episodes, in-band n = 40.** The incumbent (fp32) step-1,000

the clustered label-permutation null gives `p(macro ≥ observed) = 1.0000`. Per class: `LANE_KEEP`

The EMA+bf16 arm (ep2) emits `TURN_R` on 25/140, reaching accuracy 0.675 / macro 0.377

### `D-REFAV1-TAC-LABEL-SHARE` — ⚠️ **CORRECTS the R28 brief and inverts its lever ordering**



**MEASURED.** The R28 brief read the decoder's supervision as 0.1–0.8 % of the loss from

`loss_feat_tac`. That is the tactical **FIELD PREDICTOR's** MSE — a different term. The decoder's

own term is `w_tac_label · mean(CE_lat, CE_lon)` and on the 140 eval windows it is **0.11313

(incumbent) / 0.11695 (ep2)** against feature terms summing to **0.71918 / 0.45324** — i.e.

**13.59 % / 20.51 %** of the label+feature sum. `w_tac_label = 0.1` in both recorded configs and the

live ep2 run passed real `--labels`. ⇒ **"the head is unsupervised / the term is too weak" is

REFUTED, and raising `w_tac_label` is NOT the lever.** Two further reads settle the mechanism:

`CE_lat = 0.8665 nats` sits **BELOW** the in-band label entropy `H = 1.0944` (the head carries

0.228 nats beyond the marginal *while its argmax is constant*), and the head's own

`P(TURN_L)+P(TURN_R)` ranks the label at **AUC 0.873 [0.686, 1.000]** (ep2 0.922 [0.737, 1.000])

against a no-information 0.500. **The head ranks; it does not decide.** ⇒ the lever is the DECISION

RULE (class-balanced / focal CE), not the weight. Evidence: `raw/intent_probe_*.json`, `RESULT.md` §2.



### `D-REFAV1-TAC-NAV-ECHO` — every scrap of the tactical decision is oracle nav, not scene



**MEASURED, and it discharges the standing nav-shuffle obligation (`refa_v1.py:395`).** With

`nav_zero`, the incumbent's `CE_lat` rises 0.8665 → **1.3390** (ep2 0.9420 → 1.3684) — **above** the

marginal entropy 1.0944 — and its turn-ranking AUC collapses **0.873 → 0.520**. The longitudinal

head collapses to `CRUISE` 140/140 (accuracy 0.450 = the base rate, macro 0.200 = 1/K). A predictor

reading **nothing but `nav_cmd`** (leave-one-episode-out) scores **0.684** on the same 38 scorable

in-band rows — **above the model's 0.650 and above the constant control's 0.650.** ⚠️ `nav` is an

**ORACLE (ego-future)** derivation, training-input only. ⇒ The one signal the tactical head has

learned to read is the one that will not exist at deployment. ep2 alone retains a vision-borne

component (`nav_zero` label-TURN AUC **0.858 [0.667, 1.000]**, CI excluding 0.500).

Evidence: `raw/decode_audit.json`, `raw/intent_probe_*.json`, `RESULT.md` §6.



### `D-REFAV1-TAC-LABEL-SPARSITY` — the head sees ~2 labelled rows per batch-8 step



**MEASURED (this slice) / INFERRED (train corpus).** `s2_labels_v7.2_train.jsonl.gz` carries

### `D-REFAV1-CHORD-INSUFFICIENT` — ⚠️ **CORRECTS BACKLOG R29's framing**



**MEASURED, 0 GPU, on ep2's 25 already-curved-goal windows.** `chord = √(2(1−cos))` is strictly

monotone in `1−cos`, so it cannot change the goal term's own ordering; what it changes is that

term's **leverage inside the cost SUM**, by a measured **median 5,792.6× (conv A) / 4,096.0×

(conv B)**. That flips **1 of 25** windows under convention A and **0 of 25** under B. As shipped

the turn wins **0/25** under both. The deeper reason: on **17/25** (A) and **21/25** (B) windows the

canonical turn's goal term is **no better than constant velocity** — the direction is wrong, not

only the magnitude (see `D-REFAV1-SEED-GOAL-MISMATCH` for why). The goal term's κ-range is

**1.63e-10 (f64)** against the `0.05·κ²` penalty's **2.00e-03** — a factor **1.2 × 10⁷**, of which

the chord's √ recovers ~2 × 10³. ⚠️ And because the cost is a SUM, swapping the metric while holding

`0.05` fixed is **not a one-variable arm**: it is a metric change *and* an implicit 5,793×

reweighting. ⚠️ **SCOPE: the banked panel predates the steer-conversion repair** (`4139203`, same

day), whose tiny-model evidence puts the units-FIXED turn advantage at **+5.364e-07** (vs

**−2.384e-07** half-applied). Chord-transformed, that value would clear the 3.200e-04 charge by

**2.33×** — but on a TINY MODEL, not these checkpoints. The two readings disagree and only the

0-GPU E0 arm on the real checkpoints settles it. ⚠️ The κ² penalty is also not the only charge — the `0.02·jerk²` term from the

canonical control's own longitudinal step has mean **1.695e-04** and max **3.218e-03**, exceeding

the curvature charge on 2/25 windows. ⇒ **R29 is NECESSARY but far from SUFFICIENT and must be

declared jointly with the goal:penalty balance.** Evidence: `raw/turn_decomposition_{A,B}.json`,

`RESULT.md` §9.



### `D-REFAV1-TAC-LOSS-UNINSTRUMENTED` — the mandated term has no instrument

ActSWM anchored read `d(a) = ẑ_{t+1}(a) − ẑ_{t+1}(0)`, at h = 1 on the T1 read's own **140 windows**

(20 eval-slice episodes, `k_loader = 30`, stride 10; loader REUSED from `refav1_arm.py:483`), with

the lateral channel at ±{0.02, 0.05, 0.1} with a = 0, and a ∈ ±{0.5, 1.5} m/s² with lateral = 0.

not a curvature — `physicalai.py:621` writes `arctan(wheelbase·curvature)` into it and

independently 2 min after this run finished). **No number changes:** separation is invariant under

a monotone reparametrisation, σ is measured in the same channel (so 0.1 ≈ 2.1σ is exact), and

`tan δ ≈ δ` to 0.34 % over this range, so linear-in-steer is linear-in-curvature to the three

figures quoted. Equivalent true curvatures at the register's UNVERIFIED L ≈ 2.9 m are ≈ 0.0069 /

0.0173 / 0.0346 rad/m (R ≈ 145 / 58 / 29 m). Verdict space = `tac`

(the planner's own cost space, `_tac_field`); **all three spaces agree on both checkpoints**.

κ-axis `F_sep` **5,962.49** vs null p95 2.595 (incumbent) and **29.91** vs 2.545 (clean epoch);

a-axis 3,831.33 vs 3.696 and 102.29 vs 3.235. Exact full-field mean-displacement norms scale as

**1 : 2.500 : 5.005** and **1 : 2.498 : 4.980** against κ levels 1 : 2.5 : 5 (Spearman ρ = +1.000

both), with cos(m(+L), m(−L)) = −0.9956 … −0.9999. **Every control at its known value:** C0

identity and the zero-model control **exactly 0.0**; the zero anchor exactly 0.0; scene spread

4.2492 / 0.089146; the 200-permutation label null measured at median ≈ 1.0, p95 2.5–3.7; and the

**shuffled-ACTION control collapses the realised κ separation 27.90 → ≤ 1.83 and 16.21 → ≤ 1.86**.

carry `speed_channel: false` (verified in `ckpt_ep2\config.json` and the incumbent's `ckpt['cfg']`),

Mechanism as far as the log shows: an outlier batch (loss 1.07–1.28 before the update) whose backward overflows under bf16; `clip_grad_norm_` on an `inf` total norm scales every gradient by 0 (a finite element → 0, an `inf` element → NaN) and `opt.step()` runs anyway — a momentum-only step at best, a NaN model at worst (the trainer's own non-finite refusal would then end the run and the supervisor relaunch from the last 1,000-step checkpoint). **Guard (D-REFAV1-SKIP-NONFINITE, tested on the mirror):** `--skip-nonfinite` (default OFF, byte-identical old path) drops the batch and counts it (`skipped_steps` in every row) when the pre-clip norm is non-finite — GradScaler semantics for a precision that has no scaler; tests pin: the poisoned step leaves every tensor EXACTLY unchanged, the run continues finite, without the flag the same step NaNs the model and the trainer refuses (SystemExit), and without an event the flag is inert. Ships to Thor as supervisor v4 at the next checkpoint (pod-side switcher, supervisor v3 killed FIRST, `.PRE_SKIP` kept). **Pre-registered fallback:** if non-finite + > 1e3 events exceed 5 per 5,000 steps (drift check v3.2 counts them STICKILY over the run) or a NaN loss appears, restart from the last checkpoint under `--precision fp32 --tf32` at the 6× time cost. ⛔ **C-REFCV3-EVAL-PRIOR-LEAK — THE IN-TRAINING EVAL LEAKED THE HELD-OUT SPLIT'S LABEL MARGINALS INTO THE MODEL; FOUND BY THE SAVE-BEFORE-EVAL TEST, GATED 2026-09-02 (MEASURED on the synthetic rig; ESTIMATED magnitude on the pod).** `compute_losses_v3` called `model.core.update_tactical_prior(lat_k, lon_k)` UNCONDITIONALLY (`refc_v3_train.py:458`), and the eval reuses `compute_losses_v3`, so every eval EMA'd the held-out split's lat/lon class distribution into `core.lat_log_prior` / `core.lon_log_prior` — buffers that shape decodes through `logit_adjust` (`refc.py:2198`). `refc.py:1867`'s own docstring forbids it, and the v1 trainer gates the identical call on `model.training` (`refc_train.py:521`). ESTIMATED on the pod: momentum 0.99 × 8 eval batches → each eval moved the prior ~7.7 % toward the held-out distribution; 34 evals so far. Consequences: (1) `eval_lat_tac`/`eval_lon_tac` were partly self-referential (the prior they decode with had seen their labels' marginals) — a MARGINAL leak (3-way class frequencies), not per-window labels, so small, but eval-split information inside the deployed model; (2) the checkpoint's prior buffers carry it — the training-only EMA erases it within ~460 train batches after the gate lands (0.99^460 ≈ 1 %). **The gate (`if model.training:`) is applied**, the strict xfail that pinned the leak is flipped to a positive assertion, refc subset **218 passed / 4 skipped / 0 xfailed**. Same family as REF-A I-JEPA's val leak and the C6 confound: something the eval measures also feeds the thing being measured.

✅✅ **D-REFCV3-EVAL-DEATH-DIAGNOSED — R5 CLOSED: THE SILENT DEATHS ARE KERNEL OOM KILLS OF A 50 GB CGROUP WHOSE BUDGET IS 40 % UNRECLAIMABLE SHMEM, TRIGGERED BY THE EVAL'S MAIN-PROCESS DECODE; EACH COSTS 500 STEPS ONLY BECAUSE THE SAVE FOLLOWS THE EVAL (MEASURED on the pod 2026-09-02 19:54–19:57Z; PI go).** Evidence: memory cgroup v1 `limit 49,999,998,976` = `max_usage_in_bytes` (the cap has been hit), `memory.oom_control: oom_kill 24` — the kernel has SIGKILLed processes in this container 24 times, which is why `train.stderr.log` is empty at every death (a signal kill writes no Python traceback); `memory.stat`: **shmem 19.8 GB**, rss 16.9 GB, mapped_file 6.6 GB, cache 32.6 GB, swap 0. `/dev/shm` (24 GB) holds **six 2,359,296,064-B and six 943,718,464-B `torch_<workerpid>_*` segments = the six loader workers' in-flight fp32 batches**: 20 × 8 × 9 × 256 × 640 × 4 B window tensor + 20 × 20 × 9 × 256 × 640 × 4 B future-frames tensor = 3.3 GB per worker; dead-PID leftovers are only 24 files / 0.9 GB — **design, not a leak**. The in-training eval (`refc_v3_train.py:1102–1128`) decodes 8 × 20-window batches in the MAIN process (`num_workers=0`) on top of that; when the transient lands on a cgroup at its cap the kernel kills the largest process — the trainer (main rss 5.3 GB + a worker at 8.2 GB). It is probabilistic (page-cache state): the run **PASSED the 17,000 boundary at 20:05:53Z** on the relaunch (checkpoint written, no new kill, `oom_kill` still 24) after dying there at 19:19Z. **The cost lever is the ORDER**: the eval block precedes the `torch.save` block (`:1130`), so a death inside the eval at step N loses N−500…N. Deaths: 1,250 (a CUDA OOM with a traceback — different class), 2,000, 4,500, 6,000, 10,500, 17,000. **Fixes, ranked:** (1) save BEFORE eval + a logged try/except around the eval so a catchable error never takes the run down — patch + tests in progress, ships at the next checkpoint on the PI's go (cost of a death → ~0 steps); (2) ship in-flight batches as **uint8** and convert on the GPU — shmem 19.8 → ~5 GB, removes the pressure (loader change; next relaunch or next run, pre-registered); (3) `--workers 4` (−6.6 GB shmem) costs throughput on the 7.65-CPU quota — not first; (4) fewer eval batches shortens the transient, same peak. Same family as the CLAUDE.md `usage_in_bytes` / dense-windowed-tensor traps: a budget consumed by something unreclaimable, read as free. **First eval under the v7.2 nav (step 17,000, MEASURED):** loss 8.608, traj **1.089** (16,500: 1.169), lat_tac **1.027** (1.070).

Traps caught and pinned in the tool: WDDM over-commit ("22.49 GiB allocated" on an 8 GB card — capped by `--mem-fraction`); Kineto's GPU-side annotation copies double-count as kernels; pinned offload dies at ≈ 7 GB. ⚠️ **Recipe correction (MEASURED): a `/c/...` PYTHONPATH is not a Windows path — `import tanitad` then routes to the G: editable install; use `C:/...`.** ⛔ **Nothing applies to the live run.** PI decisions: (1) a ≈ 10-min profile on Thor (`--arms sweep,components`) would settle the bf16 ratio but ADDS GPU LOAD to a training box — the rule says no; default = wait for a checkpoint boundary or the run's end; (2) pre-register a 500-step fp32-vs-bf16 A/B (loss, gnorm, participation, `tgt_std_*`, and the Thor lever-ladder's finding that TF32 moved learned tensors) before any bf16 launch line.

✅ **D-REFAV1-EMA-SPEED — THE EMA TEACHER (#3) AND THE SPEED CHANNEL (#5) ARE IMPLEMENTED, PINNED, AND DEFAULT-OFF; THE LIVE RUN IS UNTOUCHED (2026-09-02, ArchInf FlyWheel; 197 refa tests, full suite without regression).** **EMA teacher** (`ema_targets`): `_EmaTargetPath` holds `requires_grad=False` copies of EVERY trained module on the target side — `adapter`, `tac_queries`, `tac_pool`, `strategic.read` — because an EMA adapter under a live `tac_pool` would still let the target follow the student (the brief said "adapter + subspace"; the code said otherwise, and the code won). `tq`, `st` and the strategic-extension target come from the teacher under `no_grad`; the student `tgt` still feeds the anti-collapse terms, the cf term and the participation monitor (they MEASURE the student). `model.ema_update(step, total)` lerps with a linear `0.996 → 0.999` schedule (I-JEPA ends at 1.0 — a named deviation of no practical effect); the trainer calls it after `opt.step()` behind `--ema-targets`, logs `ema_decay`, and filters the optimizer by `requires_grad` so the teacher can never receive weight decay. **Load-bearing test:** zeroing all four student modules leaves `tgt_std_tac`/`tgt_std_str` bit-identical — the target does not move with the student. **Speed channel** (`speed_channel`, PI ruling D-VELOCITY-AT-CYCLE-TIME): `augment_actions(controls, v0)` builds the predictor input `(a, κ, v_k/30)` with `v_k = v0 + Σ_{j<k} a_j·op_dt` — INTEGRATED, never indexed; it REFUSES a pre-widened tensor and a missing `v0`. `a_dim` stays **2 = control width**; `a_in_dim = a_dim + speed_channel` is the predictor input width; `forward(..., v0=)`, `plan()` (per candidate, from the tick's `v0`) and the cf negatives (re-integrated from the row's own `v0`) all use one path. Loader emits `v0 = v[2t]` at the anchor — no future speed. Both are NEXT-RUN arms; nothing here changes the Thor run.

FIX (in implementation, same owner as `refa_v1.py`): when `goal_field is None`, build it from the TACTICAL brain's own imagined field at the operative horizon — vision + nav + measured `v0` only, no future GT — and change the baseline tie-break to prefer `hold_v0` (constant speed, zero curvature) over the last candidate. (2) **the corpus was on MooseFS network storage** — MEASURED random read **301 MB/s** (≈2.2 s/step of pure IO) with **GPU at 0 % across five samples** and workers blocked. Local overlay measures **1790 MB/s random read / 4.0 GB/s write** — ~6×. Both splits copied local (172 GB used, 129 GB free); GPU went **0 % → 100 %** and step time **10.3 → 4.74 s/step**. (3) **What remains is PNG decode**, and it is CPU-capped: the quota is **7.65 cores** (`cfs_quota`, not the 96 `nproc` claims). ⇒ **~53 h for 40,284 steps.** ⚠️ **Batch size cannot fix this**: one epoch is 805,687 windows × ~28 frame-decodes regardless of batch, so the epoch's decode bill is fixed and only CORES or a cheaper codec move it. ⛔ **CONSEQUENCE FOR THE PI'S TWO ASKS:** "one full epoch" and "cover the 26 h" are **incompatible on this pod** — one epoch is ~53 h; ~26 h buys ~0.5 epoch. The levers are: accept ~53 h, move to a higher-CPU pod, or cut steps. ⚠️ And the H−F pair doubles whichever is chosen.



⛔⛔ **D-REFCV3-EVAL-LEAK — TRAINING ON "ALL OF B1" WOULD HAVE TRAINED ON 141 OF THE 147 EVAL CLIPS (caught 2026-09-02, before launch).** MEASURED: the v7.2 release splits **4,572 train / 147 eval, intersection ZERO** — but the raw B1 corpus is **4,713 = 4,572 + 141 of those eval clips** (the missing 6 are the val40 clips the parity gate drops). The armed chain pointed `--v2-cache` at all 4,713. ⇒ **every held-out number would have been optimistic, and the leak would not have announced itself — the eval would simply have looked good.** FIX: a new gate 5 builds a symlink split (`refcv3_make_split.py`, no 160 GB copy) and the trainer REFUSES if any episode id appears in both caches — *"a held-out split that is not held out measures memorisation"*. Verified on the partial corpus: train 2,132 / eval 62, **intersection 0**, eval labels md5 `aa12c948…` (canonical). ⭐ **AND THE EVAL STEP ITSELF (PI: "an eval step at 100 step with the eval split")** — every 100 steps over a FIXED held-out subset, logged as `eval_*`. ⛔ **ITS FIRST RUN WAS SILENTLY BROKEN AND THE FIX IS THE INTERESTING PART:** `shuffle=False` gives fixed windows, but takes them from the START of the first episodes (window NOW ≈0.7–2 s) while every v7.2 record is anchored at **t0 = 8.0 s ± 2 s** — so `eval_lat_tac` read **exactly 0.0000**: an eval that never measured the tactical heads while reporting a clean number. Fixed with a SEEDED random subset (fixed across steps, drawn from the whole corpus): `eval_lat_tac` **1.93**, `eval_lon_tac` **2.12** — both at ln(8)=2.08 as an untrained 8-class head must be — with `eval_tac_label_rows` and identical `eval_windows` per step. ⚠️ **SCOPE:** this is an in-training MONITOR at T0 on the same loss surface. It is NOT the four-metric-family result and may never be quoted as one; the binding families with paired episode-cluster CIs remain a separate T1 job. What it buys is seeing generalisation move DURING a 25 h run instead of after it.

⭐ **D-REFAV1-VAL-VERIFIED + TWO STALE CLAIMS IN THE LINE ABOVE, CORRECTED (2026-09-02).** **(1) THE VAL CACHE IS GOOD, AND THE PUBLISHED BAND IS NOT A PER-FILE GATE.** Re-verified at n=48 (`/home/nvidia/data/dinov3-val600-fp8-w120-256x640cyl`, 600 files / 37 GB, Thor idle at the time): **48/48 `float8_e4m3fn` with trailing shape `[640, 1024]`**, and **zero** near-zero payloads — so there is no quantisation collapse, which is the failure that would actually matter. `mean|x|` distributes **min 0.2000 · median 0.2074 · p95 0.2128 · max 0.2177 · sd 0.0039**. ⚠️ **The banked reference band `0.198–0.214` has its upper edge at roughly p95**, so a few percent of *healthy* clips exceed it by construction: a first 12-sample draw scored "3 FAIL" and the 48-sample draw scores **1/48 (2 %)**, the outlier being 0.2177 — about **one sd** out, with correct dtype and geometry. ⇒ **the band is a DISTRIBUTION-level check and is inadmissible as a per-file gate**; used as one it would reject good payloads, and "fixing" the rejects by regenerating them would burn GPU to replace healthy data. Quote it as `median 0.2074 ± 0.0039 (n=48)`, and gate per-file on **dtype, geometry and non-collapse** instead. *(Same family as the four estimator failures of 2026-08-22: a statistic quoted outside the scope that produced it.)* **(2) THE LOADER JOIN IS NOT A GAP — IT IS IMPLEMENTED.** MEASURED 2026-09-02 by reading source and running the suite: `refav1_loader.py` already performs the v7.2/nav join (`labels_path`/`nav_path`, `lat_label`/`lon_label`/`route_label`, `-100` for out-of-band windows, the ±2.0 s in-band rule derived rather than defaulted), and the model side already handles it — `refa_v1.py:991` masks with `lbl[lbl != -100]`, range-checks only the labeled rows, **skips an all-ignored family rather than averaging it to NaN**, and `F.cross_entropy` supplies `ignore_index=-100` by default; the route path at `:1010` is identical. ⛔ **The loader's own docstring still warns "THE MODEL SIDE MUST MASK … currently REFUSES negative labels" — that is STALE**, describing the state before the fix the file now sits beside. **Suite: 169 refa/refav1 tests pass**, the single failure being `test_decision_check.py` reading `MODEL_REGISTRY.md NOT FOUND` because the off-Drive mirror lacks `Project Steering/` — a mirror-incompleteness artifact, not a code failure. **(3) COMPUTE PLACEMENT IS ALSO STALE:** the k=8 control **finished** and Thor is **idle** (GPU 0 %, zero training processes). ⇒ refav1's remaining blocker is neither data nor the join nor Thor; it is a launch decision. *(This is the stale-blocker class the operating standard names: a blocker line not revisited after the thing that blocked it landed — the fourth instance, and the reason the read-set count had to be pinned by a test.)*



⭐ **D-ONE-EPOCH — EVERY NEW TRAINING RUNS ONE FULL EPOCH FROM NOW (PI 2026-09-02).** Replaces the 30,000-step default, which the v3 design had chosen deliberately (*"still under one epoch"*) and which MEASURES as **0.74 epochs** on B1. **MEASURED basis:** 170.95 windows/episode (60-episode probe → 10,257 windows) × 4,713 episodes = **805,687 windows** ⇒ at batch 20 one epoch = **40,284 steps** ≈ 24.6–29.1 h depending on the true uncontended step time. refcv3's chain is re-armed at 40,284. ⛔⛔ **40,284 IS NOT A PORTABLE CONSTANT — it is corpus-AND-batch-specific**, and copying it onto another arm would be the derived-constant-out-of-scope error this programme has paid for repeatedly (the `HORIZON = round(6.0*10/STRIDE)` case). One epoch = windows ÷ batch, so: **refcv3 B1 @b20 = 40,284** · ~~refav1 B1 @b8 = 100,711~~ **refav1 B1 @b8 = 21,109** · a v7 arm on the 2,400-episode parity corpus (415,002 windows, MEASURED in the k8 launch log) @b8 = **51,875**. ⇒ **recompute per arm at launch; never inherit the number.**



⛔⛔ **AND THE refav1 FIGURE IN THIS VERY SENTENCE WAS ITSELF THE ERROR IT WARNS ABOUT — CORRECTED 2026-09-02, 4.8× WRONG, caught by the PI asking *"why 100,711 for the same data when refcv3 is 40,000?"*** The 100,711 was computed as **refcv3's 805,687 windows ÷ refav1's batch 8** — i.e. it inherited the WINDOW COUNT and varied only the batch, which is the derived-constant-out-of-scope error one level in. ⭐ **The two arms window the SAME episodes completely differently, MEASURED from each loader's own output:** refcv3 **170.9 windows/episode** (805,687 ÷ 4,713) vs refav1 **36.9** (168,873 ÷ 4,571) — a **4.63× gap**. **Two compounding causes, derived from config and reproducing the measurement to <1 %:** (a) refav1 trains on the **0.2 s grid** (every 2nd frame), so ~199 frames become ~101 — half the starts before anything else; (b) its window spans far more of the episode — `op_window 4 + op_steps 30` = 34 grid steps (6.0 s of rollout) **plus** a strategic extension reaching another 6.0 s = 30 grid steps, so ~**64 of ~101** frames are consumed per window, against refcv3's 28 of 199. Predicted starts/episode: refav1 ~37 (measured 36.9), refcv3 172 (measured 170.9). ⇒ **one epoch for refav1 is 21,109 steps = 5.4 days** at the measured 21.95 s/step, **not 25.6 days**. ⚠️ **The rule was right and the number beside it was made the way the rule forbids** — the same shape as the `w120` docstring that labelled its own input INHERITED and concluded from it anyway. **A window count is not a property of the corpus; it is a property of the corpus AND the windowing.** ⚠️ **CARVE-OUT — the running k=8 clip-0.5 control STAYS AT 30,000.** It exists to attribute the k=60 arm, which ran 30,000; matching step counts is the whole point of a control, so "all new trainings" cannot reach back into a matched pair without destroying it. ⚠️ **AND THE DOMINANCE PAIR MUST MOVE TOGETHER:** the refcv3 claim rests on H−F with `config_delta` pinned to {hier, graft_target_latent}; raising steps on H alone would make the delta a comparison across different sample budgets — exactly the confound that pin exists to prevent. Both arms run 40,284, sequentially (35.91 GB × 2 = 71.8 GB does not fit one 44.3 GB A40), so the pair is ~50–58 h of pod time.



⛔⛔ **C-POOL-RECYCLE — `max_tasks_per_child` DEADLOCKED THE B1 BUILD THREE TIMES, AND TWO OF MY DIAGNOSES WERE WRONG BEFORE ARITHMETIC SETTLED IT (2026-09-02).** Signature each time: every worker gone, parent parked in `futex_wait_queue`, process **still "alive" to `ps`**, log frozen (once for ~2 h). ⭐⭐ **WHAT SETTLED IT WAS NOT A THEORY BUT THREE DATA POINTS FITTING ONE FORMULA** — each run hung after PRECISELY `workers × max_tasks_per_child` tasks: **48 workers → 384** new episodes (48×8), **8 workers → 64** (8×8), **6 workers → 48** (6×8). That is the exact moment EVERY child reaches its task limit and the pool must recycle them all at once. Fix: **remove `max_tasks_per_child`**. VERIFIED — the build ran 496 → 544, straight past the boundary that had stopped it three times. ⚠️ **MY TWO WRONG DIAGNOSES, both ACTED ON, are the real lesson:** (1) *fd exhaustion* — plausible (soft limit was 1024) and REFUTED by raising it to 65,536 and stalling again with 12 fds open and 436 GB free; (2) *submit-everything-at-once* — I chunked into 200-task executors and it stalled anyway, because the hang happens INSIDE the first chunk. ⇒ **A cause that explains the symptom is not the cause; a cause that predicts the NUMBER is.** Both wrong fixes were shipped before the evidence justified them, and each cost a stall. ⭐ Kept anyway because both are independently correct hardening: chunked executors bound the blast radius, and `sup_b1build.sh` restarts on **NO PROGRESS, never on liveness** — the failure mode is a process that stays alive and does nothing, which every liveness check on earth reports as healthy. The launch chain's gate 1 carried the identical flaw and now watches the file count.

The `≤85 M` band tests still guard the DEFAULT config (unchanged); the base rung is pinned separately so the override cannot drift.

The *unselected* corpus (B1, an availability accident) preserves **26.3 %** of that regime. | **MEASURED — the parity corpus cannot address the longitudinal defect; B1 IS a designed corpus with one stratum unfilled** | ⚠️ **SCOPE (PI, 2026-08-30): r0 is HISTORY.** B1 is the relevant corpus and the r0 speed-gate finding is retained as provenance for published parity numbers only, not as a live criticism. | ⛔⛔ **CORRECTED 2026-08-30 — MY "B1 WAS NOT SELECTED" CLAIM WAS WRONG, AND THE PI'S MEMORY WAS RIGHT.** B1 **IS** the product of a designed, PI-ordered stratified selection. `…/2026-08-06-alpamayo-augmentation/DESIGN.md` records the directive verbatim — *"select **100 hours** of well-distributed PhysicalAI-AV data (highway/urban/intersections, day/night, structured/unstructured…)"* — with the plan *"stratified 18,000-clip selection (**equal-weight cells over road-class × day/night × country**, proportional fill, seed 0, manifest committed)"*. ⚠️ **The error's mechanism, worth naming: the DataFlyWheel correctly measured B1 == the Alpamayo record set and I read that as "no selection" — but THE SELECTION HAPPENED ONE LEVEL UP**, in choosing which clips to send for labelling. **MEASURED** (`stack/tanitad/data/alpamayo_records.py`, `records.parquet`

sha256 `ecae276db9969de1…`, 23,644 rows):



| task | rows | coverage | status before today |

|---|---|---|---|

| `meta_action` | 4,729 | 100 % | ⚠️ I stated it was "NOT reachable locally" |

| `cot` | 4,729 | 100 % | the only field the pipeline used |

| `auto_labeling` | 4,729 | 100 % | unused |

| `vqa` | 4,722 | 99.9 % | unused |

| `grounding_via_vqa` | 4,411 | 93.3 % | unused — **2D boxes** |



**Corpus = 4,729 clips x 20 s = 26.3 hours.** The PI's recollection of "~20 h

augmented and pushed to HF" is CONFIRMED; the dataset is

`Sayood/tanitad-alpamayo2-augmentation`. My "the amount of data with Alpamayo is

limited" described the 801-clip s2 subset — a restriction I imposed — and was

reported as a property of the dataset. See RETRACTION_LOG C142.



**What each source is good for (MEASURED, not assumed):**



* `meta_action` **lateral** — 69.9 % vs 41.6 % chance, **lift x1.68**, n=1,584.

  The best lateral corroborator. (The "at chance" verdict was n=16.)

* `meta_action` **longitudinal** — monotone and magnitude-bearing:

  Strong Decel −5.88 · Gentle Decel −1.73 · Maintain +0.03 · Gentle Accel +1.93

  · Strong Accel +6.00 m/s. **Cohen's d = 1.59** accel vs decel.

  ⚠️ `Stop` is a STATE (v0 = 1.11 m/s, 66.7 % already below 1 m/s), NOT a

  deceleration — mis-mapping it is most of why a naive 4-way agreement read

  30.7 %.

* `auto_labeling.ego_vehicle_motion_analysis` — **97.1 % parse** into typed,

  time-stamped segments. Value is TIMING and VOCABULARY (EVADE / TAKE_EXIT /

  YIELD / CREEP), NOT axis agreement (55.2 %, lift only x1.16).

* `critical_components_analysis` — names the forcing object, and

  **`type: none` on 853 clips is an explicit clean negative**, the first source

  in the programme that separates "no obstacle" from "no statement".

* `grounding_via_vqa` — **the fusion gate**. 93.3 % of clips carry boxes

  (Car 2,292 · Pedestrian 1,079 · traffic light 889), so a CoT token can be

  checked against image-space perception instead of believed.

* `vqa` — ⛔ **NOT dense enough to label from.** A sampled bank: ~5 questions per

  clip, so any single question covers ~0.3 % of the corpus. Spot-checks only;

  treating it as a dense feature would fabricate coverage.



⚠️ **The anchor differs: Alpamayo `t0_us` = 5.1 s, our s2 anchor = 8.0 s.** Every

cross-source statistic published before today compared moments 2.9 s apart.

## D-REFCV4-NAV-WIRING — nav reaches ONE layer, not three (2026-09-04, Arch+Inference)



**Full design + audit: `Project Steering/DESIGN_REFCV4_NAV_WIRING.md`.** Every

claim below carries `file:line` there, re-pinned by CONTENT against the current

`refc.py` (2,477 lines) / `refc_v3.py` (1,270 lines) — both moved during the audit.



**ASSERTED (MEASURED, source read).**

* The CORE's two decision heads are strictly `f(pooled)` — vision only. `route_head

  = nn.Linear(feat, 3)` on `pooled` (`refc.py:1955`, called `:2278`); `tac_in =

  pooled` because `tactical_speed_input = False` (`refc_v3.py:447`). **Nav reaches

  neither.**

* Nav enters at exactly ONE place: the measurement encoder, `meas_in = ([v, nav] +

  ...)` (`refc.py:2273-2275`), and `m` reaches the DECODER (`:2364`) and, through

  `cond_proj(m)` (`:1503`), the selector's anchor confidence. **Nav is present in

  the operative path and absent from both decision heads** — the inversion of the

  hierarchy's thesis.

* `route_head`'s output reaches NOTHING downstream: `graft_route = False`

  (`refc.py:2341-2342`, `:1643-1644`). It is a dangling aux.

* E13's nav injection into `ctx` is a rebind of the HOOK'S LOCAL parameter

  (`refc_v3.py:861`); the hook returns only `{maneuver_logits, target_latent}`

  (`:968-969`), so the decoder still receives the un-nav'd `ctx` built at

  `refc.py:2190`. **The nav-augmented `ctx` never leaves the hook.**

* The live 40,284-step arm runs with `--nav-from-v7` OFF, `--goal-str`/`--graft-lan`

  OFF and `--ego-state-inject` OFF (verified in TWO files: `refcv3_b1_launch.sh:126-142`,

  `sup_refcv3.sh:62-76`). ⇒ **`str_goal_head` has NO DIRECT LOSS** — it trains only

  by backprop through the tactical FiLM — and the arm is **v3, not v4**.



**REFUTED — the standing claim was VACUOUS.** *"The route head is not a nav echo"*

rests on `paired_true_minus_shuffled_accuracy` = **0.0 [0.0, 0.0]**, n=3,622 win /

128 eps (`taniteval/results/refcv3-40284-openloop.ARM.json`), with the shuffle

changing the token on **49.89 %** of windows. The head is `nn.Linear(feat, 3)(pooled)`

and **cannot echo an input it never receives**. It is a pin on the WIRING, not a

finding about the model (C109 class: a probe that cannot fire proves nothing).

⇒ Re-label wherever quoted.



**ROOT CAUSE of the dead nav channel — a CORPUS interaction, not a wiring bug.**

`nav_command` needs `NAV_MIN_STEPS = 150` future poses (15 s) and reads to 250

(25 s) — `refb_labels.py:72-73` — while `*.v2ep` episodes are **199 frames = 19.9 s**.

Only windows with `t0 <= 4.9 s` (**28.5 %**) can ever emit left/right; on a 74 %-straight

corpus that lands at ~5 % non-follow, i.e. the MEASURED **94.6 % `follow`**

(`refc_v3_train.py:1127-1128`).



**CORRECTED SCOPE — two numbers were quoted outside their scope.**

* `45,466 / 168,910 = 26.92 %` is a **REF-A v1** figure (`refav1_loader.py` grid,

  `dt = 0.2`). The literals are banked NOWHERE (two mechanisms); the nearest artifact

  is a 20-episode slice. **REF-C v3's own in-band coverage is 41/172 = 23.84 %**

  (DERIVED on its grid), cross-checked against the banked **24.0 %** at

  `RESULT-refcv3-40284-stratified.md:361`. At +-4.0 s: **47.09 %**.

* The oft-quoted **72.08 %** reach-clamp kill rate is **REF-C-XL step-30k, 256

  anchors, 881 windows**. refcv3-40284 is 128 anchors / 4,823 windows / 6 s path.

  ⛔ **The refcv3 reach telemetry is NOT BANKED AT ALL** — `reach_frac_*` is computed

  at runtime and the shipped `refcv3_arm.py` never reads `sel_tele` (two probes).



**CORRECTED — "the selection surface is unstructured" is wrong.** MEASURED on the

arm: **50 of 128** anchors ever selected, entropy **2.8425 / 4.8520 nats (0.586)**,

modal anchor #57 at 14.8 %, oracle agreement 0.5652, and `goal_gate` has **OPENED to

0.1744** (score_absmean 4.0686). What is missing is any RANKING TERM expressing the

commanded manoeuvre: `r_terms` is **empty** (`graft_route`/`graft_goal`/`graft_cons`

all False). Oracle selection is worth **-0.0751 m [-0.0884, -0.0618]** = **17.0 %**

of deployed ADE.



**BOUNDING FACT — this work is necessary and provably NOT sufficient.** Oracle

selection (-0.0751) + oracle nav (-0.0239) = **0.099 m**, still short of the

**0.1423 m** by which the trivial hold-action control beats the model.



**CORRECTED — a 30 s strategic label IS constructible.** `s2_geom_emit_v7.py:52,59`

already emit `STRATEGIC_S = (8.0, 30.0)` and `LOOKAHEAD_S = 30.0`, and **1,882 train

manoeuvres start in [8, 30) s** (`band_census.json`). The reach exists because the

emitter reads the RAW clip (`recording_span_s` mean **139.7 s**) while the trainer's

`*.v2ep` cache is a **19.9 s excerpt**. **The horizon is not the constraint; EVENT

DENSITY is:** ≥1 event on **47.75 %** of clips, **≥2 (the PI's over-next) on 18.72 %**

= ~12.4 % of windows; median inter-event gap **8.9 s**. 43.0 % of windows have a

fully-observed 30 s horizon; the rest are right-censored at 38 s − NOW and must be

MODELLED as censored, not as negatives.



**HYPOTHESIS (pre-registered primary).** `t_bin` accuracy, not `p_man`. The v7.2 nav

command is a **per-clip constant** — it can echo *whether* a routing manoeuvre happens

and cannot echo *when*. Timing is the one strategic quantity a nav-conditioned head

cannot fake, and it is what the PI's *"within its time frame"* names. Controls that

must read known values: constant-only, nav-shuffled, `os_navzero`.



**RETIRES on execution: C-NAV-SOURCE-DIVERGENCE** (this file, above) — W0

(`--nav-from-v7` ON) aligns refcv3 to the v7.2 token and closes the contradiction.





## D-REFC-DDAUDIT — REF-C vs DiffusionDrive v1/v2 implementation audit (2026-09-05, Arch+Inference)



Evidence for every row: `TanitAD Research Lab/Architecture & Inference/Research/2026-09-05-refc-vs-diffusiondrive-audit/RESULT.md` (+ `raw/mechanism_check.json`, 201 windows / 3 clips, refcv3 @ 40,284, window-level paired SEs — a MECHANISM probe, not a benchmark number). Sources: arXiv 2411.15139v3 + `hustvl/DiffusionDrive@9b52ed0`; arXiv 2512.07745v1 + `hustvl/DiffusionDriveV2@1cd12a1`.



| id | claim / hypothesis | status | evidence |

|---|---|---|---|

| D-REFC-DDAUDIT-1 | ⛔ **REF-C's "truncated diffusion" decoder is NOT a diffusion model.** MEASURED, source + run: no noise schedule, no anchored Gaussian, no x0/DDIM update, no sampling at inference (`refc.py:1596-1603`: `x ← x_in + off`, eval noise `zeros_like`); train-only N(0, 0.1 m) jitter measured σ = 0.0994 and, injected at eval, moves the fan by **0.062 m** against **8.41 m** of deterministic classifier-pass offset (ADE −0.005, SE 0.006, n = 201). The timestep table has 3 rows and saturates: trace for steps = 8 is `[0,1,2,2,2,2,2,2,2]`. ⇒ It is an unrolled 3-pass anchor-refinement regressor; the registry wording should say so | **SUPPORTED** | RESULT.md §1.1 #1–#12, §2 Q1–Q4 |

| D-REFC-DDAUDIT-2 | ⭐ **The refinement passes are load-bearing but not convergent.** 0 → 2 passes: ADE 0–6 s 6.415 → 3.927 m (paired −2.488, SE 0.105), oracle-in-fan 3.942 → 1.721 m; beyond the trained 2: −0.20 m at k = 8 on 47 % of windows while ADE 0–2 s WORSENS 0.651 → 0.901 m; per-pass displacement 5.68 / 4.28 / 3.30 / 2.82 / 2.04 m (ratio 0.72–0.85, never → 0); endpoint spread collapses 103.7 → 81.7 (k = 2) → 42.0 m (k = 8) — mode collapse controlled by the pass count. The timestep embedding is live: forcing t_idx = 0 costs +1.48 m (SE 0.06) | **SUPPORTED** | RESULT.md §2 table + Q2/Q5/Q6 |

| D-REFC-DDAUDIT-3 | ⛔ **Selection is decided before refinement — the scored object is not the emitted object.** `sel_idx_base` (t = 0 confidence + priors, reach-masked) is identical to the steps = 0 winner on **201/201** windows for every steps ∈ {0,1,2,3,4,8}; only the v3 goal-scorer graft (reads fan geometry) moves the winner (10.9–14.4 %). DiffusionDrive scores the fan it emits (`argmax(poses_cls[-1])` on `poses_reg[-1]`). The in-source D1/S1/S1b notes were correct and the flags to fix it (`sel_refined`, `sel_score_emitted`, `sel_ce_reach`) are OFF in refcv3/v4 | **SUPPORTED** | RESULT.md §1.4 #28, §2 Q7; `refc.py:1613-1636`, `refc_select.py:11-31` |

| D-REFC-DDAUDIT-4 | ⭐ **The cross-attention is implemented but is not DiffusionDrive's.** Ours: content MHA from 128 anchor queries to 160 PV conv tokens + FiLM(measurement) (`refc.py:1096-1113`, `:1502-1509`). Theirs: trajectory-coordinate-indexed BEV grid-sample attention (samples the BEV map AT the candidate's waypoints) → agent-query MHA (30 detections) → ego-query MHA → FFN → per-layer AdaLN timestep modulation (`transfuser_model_v2.py::CustomTransformerDecoderLayer`, `blocks.py::GridSampleCrossBEVAttention`). We have 0 of the 3 grounded attentions because we have no BEV, no detector, no LiDAR | **SUPPORTED** | RESULT.md §1.3 #19–#26 |

| D-REFC-DDAUDIT-5 | **TransFuser is MISSING by construction (vision-only rule) and V2 changed nothing in the backbone** (`diffusiondrivev2/transfuser_backbone.py` 19,898 B vs 19,896 B; config adds `num_groups = 4` only). Structural loss: no metric frame for the decoder to index, no agents to attend — the LONGITUDINAL (headway/TTC) and TACTICAL grounding | **SUPPORTED** | RESULT.md §1.5 |

| D-REFC-DDAUDIT-6 | **V2's additions (intra-anchor GRPO G = 4, inter-anchor truncated advantage with collision → −1 and `clamp(min=0)·(r ≥ r_GT)`, scale-adaptive multiplicative noise, coarse-to-fine PDM-sub-score selector) are MISSING; the prerequisite — a stochastic denoising policy with a log-probability — is absent from our decoder.** `stack/tanitad/rl/` holds the estimators and the reward/selector-disjointness audit (sibling's RL-readiness deliverable) | **SUPPORTED** | RESULT.md §1.6 #37–#43 |

| H-DDA-1 | **Waypoint-indexed PV sampling (DD's grid-sample attention in perspective view, zero-init gate) beats a random-location control on oracle-in-fan AND the longitudinal family on the v7-tiny ladder.** Pre-registered both ways: separation ⇒ grounding is the lever, schedule base-size; none ⇒ PV tokens already carry the geometry, do not spend on BEV lifting yet | **OPEN — pre-registered** | RESULT.md §4 rank 1 (E-DDA-1) |

Closes ⇒ turn on in refcv4c; no change ⇒ selection is not binding at this fan quality, stop re-litigating S1 | **OPEN — pre-registered** | RESULT.md §4 rank 2 (E-DDA-2) |
